title: Ouyang Xiu's Mother Writes in the Sand
text:
Ouyang Xiu, born in 1007, became one of the greatest writers and statesmen of the Song dynasty: a master of prose and poetry, a reforming official and the author of two official histories. He started life with almost nothing.

His father, a minor official, died when the boy was about three, leaving the family poor. His mother, whose family name was Zheng, took him to live near an uncle in Suizhou. According to his biography in the official History of Song, the family was so poor that she could not afford paper and brush. Instead she cut the stems of reeds and used them to trace characters on the ground, teaching her son to write in the earth.

The boy proved a quick and devoted student. Since the family had few books, he borrowed them from wealthier neighbors and copied them out, and he found an old edition of the essays of the Tang writer Han Yu, which he studied with passion. He passed the highest civil examination in 1030 and went on to a long career at court, where he championed a plain, clear prose style and helped discover talented younger writers such as Su Shi.

The image of his mother teaching with reeds became a Chinese byword for a parent's devotion to a child's education against poverty.
lesson: Lack of money does not have to mean lack of learning. A determined parent can teach with whatever is at hand.
source: History of Song (Song Shi), biography of Ouyang Xiu
